thread:
Sara Liu: Heads up - several GPU training shards in us-west-2 are failing sync, looks like intermittent packet loss between pods in the same AZ. Jobs started failing ~08:34 UTC.
Miguel Ortiz: Oof. Any pod logs / netstat traces?
Sara Liu: Logs show repeated TCP retransmits and RSTs when shards try to handshake. model-sync gets stuck at 30% then times out.
Tanvi Patel: Checking calico logs now. I see a bunch of dropped conntrack entries with reason=Policy.
Tanvi Patel: infra-bot event: ClusterEvent(us-west-2-cluster): NetworkPolicy updated in namespace ml-prod at 08:29 UTC by deploy-bot.
Sara Liu: That timing matches. We rolled out a new namespace-level deny-egress netpol to lock down external access for ml-prod.
Dave R: Can you paste the netpol? Might be overly broad egress deny.
Sara Liu: Sure:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-tight
  namespace: ml-prod
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```

Miguel Ortiz: Plain deny-all egress at namespace scope — that will block east-west if pods rely on cross-namespace or nodeIP traffic. But why would same-namespace pods be blocked?
Tanvi Patel: Found another config: namespace annotation `k8s.cilium.io/qos-class: high` (used by our QoS shaper) being rewritten by the egress controller into an ACL rule that marks DSCP. Calico interprets DSCP-marked packets as external and our deny-egress with "to: {}" empty list is catching them.
Dave R: Ah interesting — traffic is getting DNATed/marked and then treated as egress to "external" rather than local. So the deny-all egress is overly broad when annotations cause packet rewriting.
Sara Liu: Repro steps I used: exec into pod-A and curl pod-B IP inside cluster -> immediate reset. ping to pod IP sometimes works once then drops.
Tanvi Patel: Commands I ran:
```
kubectl exec -n ml-prod pod/pod-a -- iperf3 -c <pod-b-ip> -t 5
kubectl logs -n kube-system calico-node -l k8s-app=calico-node --tail=200 | grep DROP
journalctl -u egress-controller -o cat | grep qos-class
```

Miguel Ortiz: Quick mitigation: update netpol to explicitly allow egress to pods in the same namespace and kube-system (for service mesh). e.g. add an egress rule with to: namespaceSelector: matchLabels: name: ml-prod and podSelector: {}
Dave R: Agreed. Patch example:
```
kubectl patch networkpolicy deny-egress-tight -n ml-prod --type=json -p='[{
  "op": "replace",
  "path": "/spec/egress",
  "value":[{
    "to":[{"namespaceSelector":{"matchLabels":{"name":"ml-prod"}}}],
    "ports":[{"protocol":"TCP","port":0}]
  }]
}]'
```

Tanvi Patel: I'll roll that patch as emergency fix to unstick shard sync. Also adding an allow for kube-system and nodeIPs.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-231 - ml-prod networkpolicy lockout (severity: P2)
Sara Liu: After patching, handshakes started succeeding. Model-sync recovered after ~2 minutes.
Miguel Ortiz: Follow-up: we should avoid namespace-wide deny-egress with an empty egress list if any sidecars or infra routes rewrite packets/DSCP. Make guardrails: preflight check that egress will not accidentally block intra-namespace traffic when qos annotations exist.
Dave R: Proposal: change deploy-bot to run a validation that simulates intra-namespace connectivity. If failure, fail the rollout and annotate the netpol with `redwood/insecure-egress: false` or require explicit allow rules.
Tanvi Patel: I'll add an automated check in the netpol admission webhook to query for common QoS annotations (cilium, istio, calico) and ensure allow rules exist.
Sara Liu: Also let's add a one-off script to scan clusters for other namespaces with both qos annotations + deny-egress and alert.
Miguel Ortiz: Can we add a temporary runbook entry for oncall? Steps: 1) check calico logs for Policy drops 2) kubectl get networkpolicy -n <ns> 3) if deny-egress with empty egress, patch to allow namespaceSelector 4) restart pods if necessary.
oncall-bot: Runbook updated: /runbooks/netpol-qos-interaction.md (internal) :thumbsup:
Tanvi Patel: I'll follow up with PR for the webhook and the cluster scan. Leaving the incident open until we have the webhook deployed to prod.
Sara Liu: Thanks everyone, marking jobs as OK now. :rocket:
